summary: Swift 1.5 fine-tune of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, built with the GSQ-RCO Q2_0 recipe and Swift's own routers, MTP block and tokenizer.

architecture.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Swift 1.5 fine-tune)
architecture.type: Mixture-of-experts transformer with linear-attention layers, n-gram per-layer embeddings (PLE) and a multi-token-prediction head

source.derivation: GSQ-RCO Q2_0 expert payloads, 96 router tensors restored from Swift BF16, Swift MTP block and tokenizer

quantization.label: GSQ-RCO Q2_0
quantization.dense: mixed (BF16 routers, Q3_K to Q6_K, IQ4_XS)

main.content: part 1 of a two-part split GGUF: the conversion's main GGUF with split keys added (scripts/backends/repack_split_gguf.py; tensor payloads and metadata verified identical)

ple.content: part 2: the per-layer n-gram embedding (PLE) table, IQ4_NL, streamed from disk row by row; byte-identical to the conversion's standalone PLE GGUF

vision.source: ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF@ed59f92082b1e93c0e96d60a8b11aab089b52f09 (the BF16 projector the production Q8_0 copy was made from)

memory.note: Splash's own plan for this model (/status): target weights plus the DFlash2 draft (0.49 GiB), INT8 KV at 131072 tokens, prefill/decode/state/pipeline/runtime reserves, BF16 vision. Swift's tokenizer profile qwen2 (patch 0001); the base model's BF16 projector, as Swift shares the base projector natively. Measured peak wired 43.24 GiB (whole machine, backend A/B 2026-11-13).

provenance.notes: Tokenizer uses tokenizer.ggml.pre=qwen2 with NFC normalization; requires the tokenizer-adapter runtime patch.

evidence.speed and memory: backend A/B on Splash-m1 1.6.1-m1-ds1, 2026-11-13 (short, 8K and 32K prompts, repeated prefix; temperature 0; Manifests/evidence/backend-ab)
evidence.start: lifecycle matrix on the promoted default, 2026-11-13 (idle to healthy through the Workstation service)
